editorial.headline: Other Photography Activities: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This broad photography activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks its registration there today.
editorial.body:
Photography is often treated as a simple service, but this activity has a broad working perimeter. It covers still photography and photo shoots for individuals and business purposes: passport, school and wedding work, alongside commercial, publication, fashion, real-estate and tourism photography. It also includes underwater photography and video recording for events such as weddings and meetings. The common thread is commissioned image-making for a person, an event or a commercial use—not a narrow studio-only practice.

The scope continues after the shutter. It includes processing and printing clients’ film or cine-film negatives, including washing, printing and enlarging; film-processing laboratories; and one-hour photo shops, provided these are not part of a camera store. Slide mounting, duplication, restoration and minor alteration of transparencies also sit within the activity. So do photojournalism, the creation of document microfilm, 3D-object scanning, and processing or converting photographs into digital formats before uploading them to cloud storage. It is therefore a practical category spanning capture, image handling and digital delivery.

Nationally, the activity is open to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. It is available across micro, small, medium and large business scales. That national position matters: it confirms that foreign participation is permitted for the activity as such, rather than limiting the work to a particular business size. A founder considering this category should nevertheless separate national openness from the place where the PMA registration is to be made.

In Bali, that distinction is decisive. A foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA there today. At the large scale, OSS assigns a Low or Medium-Low risk level across every scope within the activity, placing it inside Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. The block is tied to the Bali moratorium of May 13, 2026. Nationally open therefore does not mean PMA-registrable in Bali: for this activity, the provincial restriction controls the practical outcome on the island.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not translate into PMA registrability in Bali: this activity is blocked there today.
